record.title: EU Commission adopts a proposed PUE/WUE rating scheme for data centres and opens a separate minimum-standards consultation
record.summary: On 21 September 2026, the European Commission adopted delegated-regulation text C(2026)3472 final establishing a common data-centre sustainability rating scheme using reported energy and water indicators, including PUE and WUE classes. The text provides for electronic labels generated from operator-reported data, with an annual schedule beginning 15 August 2027. The Commission also opened a separate 12-week consultation on possible minimum performance standards, due 14 December 2026, with a legislative proposal planned for Q2 2027. The inspected regulation PDF still has blank final EU number and Official Journal date fields; scrutiny, entry into force, deployed labels and effects are not established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The European Commission adopted C(2026)3472 final on 2026-09-21 as delegated-regulation text establishing a common EU data-centre sustainability rating scheme based on energy- and water-related indicators including PUE and WUE.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Commission text describes electronic labels generated from operator-reported data, with an annual label schedule beginning 2027-08-15; the published PDF retains blank EU regulation number and Official Journal date fields, so final publication and entry into force are not established here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On 2026-09-21 the Commission opened a separate 12-week consultation on possible minimum performance standards, with feedback due 2026-12-14 and a legislative proposal planned for Q2 2027.

evidence_gaps.description: Formal scrutiny/OJ publication and entry into force of C(2026)3472, first deployed labels, binding minimum standards, facility capex/opex and realized energy/water savings are not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, a common PUE/WUE label and reporting pipeline could change transparency and procurement comparisons for EU data centres, while a separate prospective minimum-standards process could later alter efficiency constraints. Current evidence establishes Commission policy design and consultation, not binding effect, facility outcomes or realized energy/cost savings.
limitations: C(2026)3472 is Commission-adopted delegated-regulation text, but the inspected PDF still has blank final EU number and OJ date fields; scrutiny completion, publication and entry into force are not established.
The Commission’s PUE/WUE classes and label schedule establish policy design, not actual labels, facility compliance, efficiency investment or realized energy/water savings.
Minimum performance standards are a separate consultation and prospective legislative proposal planned for Q2 2027, not a current binding threshold.
No facility-level costs, siting changes, AI-compute constraints or economic/environmental effects were measured.

technical.demonstrated_result: The Commission’s C(2026)3472 final text sets out PUE/WUE classes and a process for electronic data-centre labels from operator-reported data; a separate Commission announcement opens consultation on possible future minimum standards.
